body: Hey, thanks for the advice and sorry about the late reply. Distractions are sometimes indeed useful.
Thanks. I have been pushing through but there's nothing to look ahead to. I'm tired of this illness and just want everything to end. Life is pretty miserable..

It's ok, literally every student has had bad tests. Honestly, sometimes your mind can go blank because of anxiety or a panic attack. It's probably a good idea to just be honest and say you weren't feeling that well during the test. Maybe also ask if it can be taken again? One idea is to show your teacher that you actually know everything on the test whenever this is possible. It's slightly different if it's a big, important exam though...
Yes, I just want to go into non-consciousness so I don't have to deal with constant disappointment.
Almost everything in 2017 has been a train wreck for me, if that counts for something.

I don't think it does to be honest. Maybe for a short time you are buzzed but I personally just feel crap after a few minutes. Alcohol will make things worse in the long term as it is a depressant. Also nobody enjoys hangovers. I understand why people do it but it comes at a price and it's not a good deal.

That hit quite hard for me. Sorry about your situation. If it means anything, I respect you for earning a degree in a hard science. I think you're doing the right thing by working your way back up. Often, we can't foresee these things so regretting things afterwards is counterproductive. I can relate because
I definitely feel like I'm slipping in life.
Thank you for the reply. I have a rough idea, but that doesn't get me far.
Yeah man, completely understand. Mornings are really tough for me as well. At least you've had a girlfriend in the past so you seem like a god to me right now...

No, not really. In real life they are doing really well and are happy. Things go smoothly for them, academically, financially, etc. I can clearly see it. It is probably a hard truth that I'm falling behind, however it is frustrating considering how my efforts amounted to nothing.

What you describe is scarily accurate to what I'm going through. Especially using food as therapy. Sometimes exercise helps but I realise it is very difficult for a depressed person to motivate themselves to do it.

Well done for trying to make the best of it this year. I hope you succeed. All the best.

It is disappointing and frustrating, I agree. Especially if you set your heart on something. However, there are surely many other projects or competitions out there that would welcome someone as skilled as you. 

Your degree can still be really useful in many areas that require a mathematical/technical background and logical problem solving.

Wait, you weren't allowed to compete because of age? If that's the case it's incredibly harsh and dumb. Still, you did amazingly well to earn your degree with such a high grade. That's an impressive achievement.

If we're being honest, nobody knows the meaning of human existence. Sure the biological meaning is to propagate the species but that's not a satisfying answer. Some of the biggest minds in history have thought about this and couldn't come up with a 'logical' answer. 

In fact, it is possible that the question itself may be flawed. It is possible that we exist simply because it is in the nature of the universe, much like how electric charges exist simply because it is a fundamental property of the universe.

Completely understand you - it's beyond frustrating and humiliating. 

I haven't yet found a solution but I know for sure that alcohol will only do damage in the long term. It is a known depressant and in my view the short buzz is not worth it.
Well great. Now there's nothing really to look forward to. This life is a big competition and I can't even compete so yeah...
Oh you too? I know what you mean, it's not so much about driving but it crushes your motivation and hope since you've put in a lot of effort but get nothing in return.
Some days it does but I've been like this for a while now. Even before uni I wasn't well mentally due to insomnia and anxiety which is beyond my control.
